subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This defines a public plugin API around security-sensitive persisted config, auth, provider, and secrets-adjacent writes, so automation cannot choose the trust boundary or failure semantics safely.

options.title: Design the API in RFC first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering, actor metadata, recursion, timeout, and fail-closed behavior in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the approved SDK contract with tests.

options.title: Rely on built-in validation only
options.body: Decide not to add a plugin veto and close or rescope this around the existing schema, SecretRef, baseHash, destructive-array, and agent-tool guards.

options.title: Limit to agent tool writes
options.body: Add a narrower gateway-tool guard for model-initiated config writes, accepting that other config writers remain outside the plugin veto path.

recommendation.title: Design the API in RFC first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering, actor metadata, recursion, timeout, and fail-closed behavior in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the approved SDK contract with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They already supplied the clearest product/security routing comment for this issue and have relevant config write history.
